If a binary function from a type equipped with a total relation `r` to a monoid is
anti-symmetric (i.e. satisfies `f a b * f b a = 1`), in order to show it is multiplicative
(i.e. satisfies `f a c = f a b * f b c`), we may assume `r a b` and `r b c` are satisfied.
We allow restricting to a subset specified by a predicate `p`.
statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [inst : Monoid β] (r : α → α → Prop) [Std.Total r] (f : α → α → β) (p : α → Prop),
  (∀ {a b : α}, p a → p b → f a b * f b a = 1) →
    (∀ {a b c : α}, r a b → r b c → p a → p b → p c → f a c = f a b * f b c) →
      ∀ {a b c : α}, p a → p b → p c → f a c = f a b * f b c

∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [inst : AddMonoid β] (r : α → α → Prop) [Std.Total r] (f : α → α → β) (p : α → Prop),

      ∀ {a b c : α}, p a → p b → p c → f a c = f a b + f b c
